name: North Coast
summary: The Atlantic-facing coast from Bude in the far north-east down to Gwithian and Godrevy on St Ives Bay, including Padstow, Newquay, Perranporth and St Agnes.
boundaryNote: Draft boundary: Devon border at Marsland Mouth to Godrevy Point. Hayle and St Ives are in West Cornwall.

name: West Cornwall (Penwith)
summary: The Penwith peninsula west of Hayle: St Ives, Zennor, St Just, Sennen, Porthcurno, Mousehole, Penzance and Mount's Bay as far east as Praa Sands.
boundaryNote: Draft boundary: Hayle estuary on the north coast to Praa Sands on Mount's Bay.

name: The Lizard
summary: The Lizard peninsula, mainland Britain's most southerly point, from Porthleven and Helston round to Coverack and the Helford River.
boundaryNote: Draft boundary: Porthleven to the south bank of the Helford River.

name: South Coast
summary: The sheltered south coast from Falmouth and the Roseland to Mevagissey, St Austell Bay, Fowey, Polperro and Looe, plus Truro on the Fal.
boundaryNote: Draft boundary: north bank of the Helford River to Seaton. Truro is included here as it sits at the head of the Fal.

name: Bodmin Moor & East Cornwall
summary: Inland Cornwall around Bodmin Moor, Launceston and Liskeard, the Tamar Valley, and the Rame Peninsula with Whitsand Bay, Cawsand and Kingsand.
boundaryNote: Draft boundary: everything east of Seaton on the south coast plus inland towns not on the north coast. Bodmin and Camelford are included here.
